Thanks again for taking time earlier today. Quick recap + next steps from our discovery call: 

- High-level SLO targets: 95th p95 latency <= 200ms for single-turn text generation at your standard 512-token prompts; 99th p99 tail <= 400ms for priority routes.
- Throughput: baseline 300 reqs/min with burst up to 1,200 reqs/min during payroll windows.
- Concurrency: expect spikes to 120 concurrent streams on the customer-facing route.
- Streaming: you require streaming token-by-token updates for the chat UI with a max tolerated stall of 50ms between packets.
- Autoscaling/burst: you asked about scale-up time and warm pools — we typically target warm-pool capacity that can handle ~50% of expected bursts, with cold scale-up time between 30–90s depending on instance type and warm-cache reuse.

Attachments: I attached the autoscale_playbook.pdf and a proposed autoscale_sla_matrix.xlsx with initial numbers. See the matrix for two rollout options (conservative / aggressive).

Next steps (owners):
1) Redwood to confirm technical sizing and expected warm-pool behavior for FastPay workload — Ethan + Dylan (ETA 48 hours).
2) FastPay to share recent 7-day peak QPS and concurrency patterns (Priya).
3) Align on an SLO/penalty-free pilot window once sizing validated (Marissa).

Let me know if I missed anything or if you want a short follow-up 20-min call to go over the playbook.

Appreciate the questions, Alex — answers below and I've looped Ethan to validate the numbers on our side. Dylan (engineering) will weigh in on exact cold-start p99 stats.

1) Warm pool sizing: we usually size warm pools by concurrency for streaming workloads. For your case I'd recommend pre-warming for ~60 concurrent streaming sessions (50% of expected peak concurrency), which roughly maps to handling ~600 reqs/min for short interactions. The attached SLA matrix includes both concurrency and req/min columns so you can see mapping.

2) Scale-up time / p99 on cold starts: historical data across comparable customers shows median cold scale p95 ~2.5s for container reuse scenarios, p99 in worst-case ~120s when new instances need full model load and KV cache warm. That worst-case is rare but possible on major bursts. We mitigate via warm pools, model shard reuse, and prioritized scheduling for priority routes.

3) Queueing behavior: Redwood will place overflow requests in a short in-memory queue (configurable per-route). Default behavior is to queue for up to 10s before returning a 429 to the client with backoff guidance; for high-priority routes we recommend an aggressive warm-pool + short queue (2–3s) to avoid user-visible retry loops.

4) Pilot: we can support a 2-week pilot with no SLA penalties while we validate the autoscale profile — Marissa will draft the pilot terms if that works for you.

Next: Ethan / Dylan — can you confirm the recommended warm-pool config (concurrency and instance counts) for the conservative and aggressive columns in the SLA matrix? We need an ETA by end-of-day Thursday.

Thanks,
Marissa
